label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hello everybody, it's Hélène from Pétrin Doré. Thomas, my nephew, showed me this thread this morning. To answer M. Bergeron and everyone else: **we are not closing. We are not moving. It's the opposite.**

I was keeping this as a surprise for the reopening, but I see the surprise is not working so well, so here is the "grande nouvelle" a few weeks early.

**We bought the building.**

The cousin of Marc-Antoine is half right. The building at the corner was sold. It was sold to me! We signed at the notary on December 15.

Many of you know M. Ferland, the owner. He is 81 and he is retiring to Sherbrooke to live near his daughter. Before he put the building on the market, he came to me first and asked if I wanted to buy it. For 17 years he has come every morning for his baguette pas trop cuite. I think he wanted to know the bakery would stay. He cried a little bit at the notary, and to be honest I did too. So no condos, no bank, no vape shop. Just the same bakery, with the same flour on the floor.

**Why we close January 4 to 18**

We are doing work. The big thing is a new deck oven, 4 decks, coming from a supplier in Laval. The old oven is from 1998 and this year it broke down 3 times. Some of you were there the morning in September when there was no bread until 10h. I don't want to live that again, and neither do you.

We are also taking the space at the back, the old storage room of the dépanneur. We will put in 6 small tables, so finally people can sit down with their coffee and croissant instead of eating on the sidewalk in February.

**We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7h in the morning.** Same hours as always after that.

**About the carnets**

M. Bergeron, you asked a straight question, so here is a straight answer.

We sold 214 carnets in October, $60 for 12 loaves. **Every carnet is still good. There is no expiry date and there will never be one.** If you have 7 loaves left on yours (hello noodle_and_crumb), you still have 7 loaves. You can use them when we reopen on the 19th, next month, next year, whenever you like.

To say thank you for your patience, **every carnet holder gets one free croissant in January.** Just bring the carnet.

And if somebody is really worried and wants their money back, come see me at the counter and I will give it back, no questions asked. No hard feelings either. I want you to feel good when you buy bread from me.

I have to say one honest thing, and then I'm done with it. When I read the word "scam", it hurt. I've been on this street 17 years. I opened in March 2009 with one oven and my sister helping on weekends. I know a lot of you by name, and I know your kids and your dogs. So yes, it stung.

But I also understand. Mile End has lost a lot of small shops in the last few years. People see a sign, half-empty shelves, a rumour about the building, and they think the worst. It's normal to worry when you love a place, and I take it as a compliment that you care this much. I just wish Thomas had written a better sign!

**About the sign and the shelves**

The sign was written by Thomas at 6h in the morning. "Grande nouvelle bientôt!" was his idea and I said ok without thinking. With the oven, the notary and the Christmas rush, my head was somewhere else. Lesson learned. Next time I write the sign myself, with full sentences, and maybe with a coffee first.

The half-empty shelves on the 28th were because we sold everything for Christmas Eve. We made 400 bûches this year (I'm still a bit tired). The shelves were empty because you bought it all, so thank you, but it had nothing to do with closing.

**For the tenants upstairs**

I know some of you living above the bakery probably read this too, and I know a building sale is scary when you rent. So I want to say it publicly: **the 3 apartments stay rented, same tenants, same rent.** I already promised this in writing to each of you, and I'm saying it here too so everybody knows. Nothing changes for you except that your new landlord is the person who makes the bread under your floor. If anything, you'll smell croissants earlier in the morning now with the new oven. Sorry in advance.

**Thank you**

Priya, thank you for defending us. Your little one can keep coming on Saturdays, the chocolatine tradition is not going anywhere. And thank you to everyone else who spoke up for us, here and on the street. Thomas told me some people stopped him outside to ask if we were ok. That means a lot.

M. Bergeron, thank you too, honestly. You asked the question politely and directly, and that's what made me sit down and write this instead of waiting until January. You were right that people deserved an answer before the 4th.

**You're all invited, Saturday January 23**

To celebrate the new oven, the new tables, and the bakery staying on Fairmount, please come by on **Saturday, January 23.** Coffee and a piece of the new bread are on the house. It's for everybody, regulars, new people, people who were worried, people who called us a scam (I won't remember who, promise). Come sit at the new tables and tell me if the pain de campagne is as good from the new oven as from the old one. Between us, I think it will be better.

And if M. Ferland makes the trip from Sherbrooke, and I hope he does, his baguette pas trop cuite will be waiting.

So the short version: we are closed January 4 to 18 for work, we reopen Tuesday January 19 at 7h, the party is Saturday January 23, your carnets are safe forever, and we're staying for a long, long time.

À bientôt, and bonne année to all of you,

Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
